subject.title: Memory compaction blocks main processing lane, causing unresponsive bot for 10+ minutes

question: Should OpenClaw move preflight compaction and memoryFlush into a dedicated or preemptible maintenance lane, or keep them in-band with shorter timeouts and recovery diagnostics?
rationale: The bug is source-reproducible and high impact, but the durable fix changes scheduler, transcript, and session-ordering semantics that automation should not choose alone.

options.title: Dedicated or preemptible maintenance lane
options.body: Move compaction and memoryFlush out of the foreground session path while explicitly preserving transcript rotation and session ordering invariants.

options.title: In-band with stronger watchdogs
options.body: Keep the current lane ownership but add a watchdog, faster abort, and visible recovery path for stuck compaction.

options.title: Timeout-only mitigation
options.body: Treat the 180s timeout, failure counters, and progress notices as sufficient for now and leave lane isolation out of scope.

recommendation.title: Dedicated or preemptible maintenance lane
recommendation.body: Move compaction and memoryFlush out of the foreground session path while explicitly preserving transcript rotation and session ordering invariants.

likelyOwner.reason: He introduced the memoryFlush feature and appears in the current central file history, making him the best available routing candidate for the scheduler/product call.
